So the Senator IS introduced in the very next sentence of the draft: "For years Adams had taught American youth never to travel without a Senator—useful in America at times, but indispensable in Russia." So the Senator is introduced/explained in the sentence immediately following. Order is: "the Senator pointed to Moscow" → "for years Adams had taught never to travel without a Senator." However, the very next sentence glosses who/what the Senator is. A competent reader would catch up immediately. **"The tragedy of King impressed Hay intensely"** (Ch 030)

Actually in the source it's "The tragedy of King impressed him intensely: 'There you have it in the face!' he said—" The "he said" is Hay speaking. The "game" = the double-standards political game. This still parses for a competent reader. Not a finding.

**Ch 030: "Hay had induced the Senate, with only six negative votes, to permit Great Britain to renounce, without equivalent, treaty rights which she had for fifty years defended tooth and nail."**

**Ch 029: "As the monkey looked back across the Baltic from the safe battlements of Stockholm, Russia looked more portentous than from the Kremlin."**

The draft goes directly from "he took steamer for Sweden and landed at Stockholm" to "Until the student is fairly sure..." to "Yet Russia was too vast a force..." to "As the monkey looked back across the Baltic..." — the monkey metaphor arrives with no establishment in the draft. A reader has no idea what "the monkey" refers to. This is a genuine dangling reference.

Let me verify: does the draft contain any prior mention of "monkey"? Searching the draft... No. The La Fontaine poem and the bear/monkey discussion ("as bear or as monkey according to the mirror he held before him") are entirely cut from the draft. The "monkey" appears from nowhere.

The authorized removals are specific listed items. The monkey/La Fontaine passage is not among them. This is a **valid finding**.
